HOW THE NUMBERS WERE MADE the rig, in plain words

The game's own client (v29.58, blob 8b3a0983…; the words, the ladders and the dials read at v29.59, which changed no pet byte) ran headless with every pet owned and ONE at heel, stood at level 1, 50 or 100 by his banked XP (the same save a player would carry). Ten seeded 90 s fights a level: campaign 10, 32 and 60, BEAR PARK 5 and DINO PARK 15, each with Sarge marching and with Sarge held back behind the line, the pistol in his hand, a squad of three riflemen and a medic. THE STANDING LAW (the house rig's, CARD-BAL): a knock is a no-op, every Green man's health is refilled each frame and Sarge's hits are capped under his cap, so the fight runs the whole 90 s against a live Tan stream and the pet's deeds are counted. THE NATURAL LAW: the same, but Sarge's hits are not capped, so a guard's block and a mender's stitch meet real hurt; on these rugs Sarge never fell all the same (his cap at commander level 30 with a medic beside him), so the guards and the menders are judged by PIPS KEPT: the hits he took without the pet minus with him, plus the pips the pet sewed. Every number is the pet's against the NO-PET run of the same seed, then the median over the ten fights. The Tan man's HP on these rugs: 4 at campaign 10, 7 at 32, 10 at 60 (a 1-pip bite is a quarter of a man on the first, a twelfth on the last: the same pet reads weaker as the Tan grow). The kit: design/pet-audit-1103/kit (read.mjs, rig/measure.mjs, rig/table.py, build.py); it re-runs on any client in about twenty minutes.
